newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes lower ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes lower ahead of holiday.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed sharply lower in thin trade ahead of the Christmas holiday, market sources said Tuesday.
"We gapped lower and the sellers were just lining up," said one dealer.
Traders cited ample power supplies, mild weather conditions and weaker natural gas prices as bearish factors for electricity.

January 1997 California-Oregon border (COB) futures closed down $4.26 per megawatt hour (MWh) at $18.79, while the February contract was down $1.00 at $17.50. Other active COB contracts were down 25 to 35 cents.
January Palo Verde closed down $2.26 at $22.00 per MWh, while February lost $1.50 to settle at $18.00. Other PV contracts were down 40 cents to $1.00.
The January electricity contracts expire Thursday.
